review_method: Each listed image was opened and visually inspected. These decisions are not inferred from prompts or supplied references.
technical_note: Some delivered images are 1704x923, not 16:9. Keep the existing final-frame aspect gate. Any technical crop must be inspected before montage. Creative acceptance below does not authorize rendering or publication.

reviews.notes: Incoming fish tray, quay inventory and rust porter outfit readable. Headband knot orientation differs from the next view; retain as a continuity caution, not a claim of exact identity.
Porter moves with the same incoming tray; unloading inventory remains visible. Minor headband directionality caution from 001.
Boatman's charcoal lower garment becomes light grey with blue cuffs and yellow straps. Grip hand is too detailed; small motion marks also need removal.
Assistant checks sleeve coins without inventing a completed sale. Indigo clothes and quay remain consistent.
Boatman's lower clothes drift. Assistant incorrectly stands behind the selling counter rather than on its street side.
Explicit fourth fish tray appears, but boatman clothes and assistant's side of counter remain wrong.
Corrected white neck and rounded hands. Mooring, canoe, landing and grower clothing retained.
Two dark-green squash and basket are consistent, but the grip still has several separate finger lobes.
Grinding room and maize action remain, but a grey skin band under the chin survived the correction.
Two green squash, basket handle and mooring restored. Basket appears smaller in this wider view; no orange squash substitution remains.
Grower takes remaining produce basket, room inventory retained and skin corrected. Partner changes from kneeling to standing as the scene progresses; document this action, not a frozen pose.
Two workers, three sacks, empty receiver doorway and dry quay readable. Woven hem less visible at wide scale; not proof of pixel-identical clothes.
Closer carrier and load inspection preserves clothing and the waiting situation.
Carrier rope moved to door-side sack rather than unused river-side sack. Loose rope loop remains visible; no completed reception implied.
Unused sacks restored to dry bank, but both workers still have crossed V-neck collars rather than their round slit collars.
Door-side sack rests flat, rope belongs to that sack, unused river-side sacks and empty boat retained.
One intact brown bowl above basket, no literal breakage. Fixed pottery room inventory retained.
Bowl lowered while maker waits; clothes and workshop inventory retained.
Second adult asks for room; potter turns while retaining the intact bowl.
Potter lifts intact bowl clear, with stable basket, padding and racks.
Round rust collar restored; maker's hands now simple white ovals. One intact bowl, padding, racks, clay block and tools retained.
Round collar restored and bowl settles intact into padding; maker moves to the bench. Risk of breakage is not illustrated as an actual broken bowl.
Plain brown laceless low shoe replaces boot variation. Customer street side and worker shop side retained; white hands simplified.
Shoe gap and simple hands are readable, but worker and customer reverse left/right compared with the specified same-camera crop. Reframe without crossing the scene axis.
Same shoe and room retained. Pointing hand still draws an individual index finger; use whole mitten direction instead.
Same laceless shoe lifted for examination, not repaired. Several grip finger lines remain and customer hand is too detailed.
Worn shoe remains on front counter, but a metal spike appears on the wooden mallet handle. Preserve a plain mallet plus two separate awls, and simplify reach hand.
Worker takes one awl, but bench mallet retains an invented metal spike and grip fingers remain detailed. Remaining inventory must be one plain mallet plus one awl.
